```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="k03" data-src="../assets/learn/data/07-cost.json ../assets/learn/data/13-capstone.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Money over time, in six moves</p>
<ol>
<li>Growth compounds: $100 at 7% a year, interest left in, is $196.72 after 10 years and first passes $200 in year 11 ($210.49). Simple interest gives $170.00 after 10 years.</li>
<li>Discounting runs it backwards: $100 paid in 10 years is worth $100 ÷ 1.07¹⁰ = $50.83 today, its present value.</li>
<li>Far-off money feels the rate most: from 7% to 4%, $100 in 30 years rises from $13.14 to $30.83 today.</li>
<li>$1 a year for 30 years at 4% is worth $17.29 today, not $30: the annuity factor.</li>
<li>The capital recovery factor is 1 ÷ 17.29 = 0.05783: the wind farm's $1,712 per kW becomes $99.01 a year for 30 years.</li>
<li>Add upkeep of $34.57: the yearly cost is $133.58 per kW, or $133,575 per MW. At 0% the factor is 1 ÷ 30 = 0.0333.</li>
</ol>
```

## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="k3-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Compound growth</dt><dd>Each year adds a percentage of what is there now, so the amount grows faster and faster: × (1 + r)<sup>t</sup>.</dd>
<dt>Present value</dt><dd>What a later amount is worth today: divide by (1 + r)<sup>t</sup>.</dd>
<dt>Annuity factor</dt><dd>What $1 a year for n years is worth today: the sum of the discounted dollars, 17.29 at 4% over 30 years.</dd>
<dt>Capital recovery factor</dt><dd>One over the annuity factor: the share of a building cost repaid each year, 0.0578 at 4% over 30 years.</dd>
<dt>Yearly cost</dt><dd>CRF × building cost + fixed upkeep: $133.58 per kW a year for the wind farm.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Where the formula comes from, and real against nominal rates</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **A stream is a geometric series.** $n$ yearly payments $A$, each discounted, add up to $\frac{A}{1+r} + \dots + \frac{A}{(1+r)^n} = A\,\frac{1-(1+r)^{-n}}{r}$. The fraction is the [annuity factor]{.lx-term term="annuity-factor"}: 17.29 at 4% over 30 years.
- **Set it equal to the building cost** $C$ (\$ per kW): $A = \frac{r}{1-(1+r)^{-n}}\,C = \mathrm{CRF} \cdot C$.
- **Two ways to write it.** Multiply top and bottom by $(1+r)^n$: $\frac{r}{1-(1+r)^{-n}} = \frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n - 1}$. [Lesson 7](07-cost.html) writes the first, lesson 13's code the second.
- **Real against nominal.** $(1 + \text{nominal}) = (1 + \text{real})(1 + \text{inflation})$. Lesson 7's illustrative blend, 7% nominal with 2.5% inflation, is 4.39% real.
- **Do not mix them.** Costs in today's dollars go with a [real rate]{.lx-term term="real-rate"}; cash in the dollars of each future year goes with a nominal rate.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The yearly cost inside a planning model (a preview)</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **One year stands for the life.** [Lessons 12](12-trade-offs.html) and [13](13-capstone.html) minimise one year's cost, $\sum_k (\mathrm{CRF}_k\, C_k + \mathrm{FOM}_k)\,K_k$ plus running costs, with $K_k$ the MW built of plant $k$.
- **Units.** $C_k$ and $\mathrm{FOM}_k$ are per kW, so the model multiplies by 1,000 for each MW: one MW of wind adds \$133,575 a year.
- **The assumption.** Every year of the life looks like the modelled year, and each plant is paid off over $n$ years at the same rate: 30 years for plants, 15 for lesson 13's battery.
- **Where next.** A model that spans decades discounts each year's cash instead, and credits plants that outlive its horizon (Modeler lesson M13, upcoming); M11 (upcoming) puts a project's full cash flow inside the optimization.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="k3-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="third" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A plant paid off over 30 years costs 1/30 of its building cost each year.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth, unless the rate is 0%. At 4% the yearly share is 0.0578, not 0.0333: lenders and owners are paid for the wait.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="halve" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Doubling the discount rate halves what $100 paid in 30 years is worth today.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. From 3.5% to 7% it falls from $35.63 to $13.14, by 63%: the rate sits inside an exponent.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="k3">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="pv20" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">What is $100 paid in 20 years worth today, at 7% a year?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">$386.97</li><li data-value="b">$41.67</li><li data-value="c">$25.84</li><li data-value="d">$50.00</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$25.84: 100 ÷ 1.07²⁰. $41.67 divides by 1 + 20 × 0.07 (simple interest); $386.97 grows the $100 forward instead.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="crf" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">Which is the capital recovery factor at 4% over 30 years?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">0.0333</li><li data-value="b">0.0400</li><li data-value="c">0.0578</li><li data-value="d">0.0806</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>0.0578. 0.0333 is 1 ÷ 30, the 0% case; 0.0400 pays the return but never the cost; 0.0806 is the factor at 7%.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="k3-drill"></div>
```
